status: PASS arbitrary-word old-bridge zipper and global cycle-erasure bound
analytic: At a block entry the stationary w cursor scans distinct ports for at most four R turns. For r<=3 the subsequent black departing edge is old. If it is still a bridge after the insertions, no new edge can reach its old far component, since all new edges originate at w and such a connection would bypass it. The post-L active edge set therefore equals the far component of the exact block-entry active component minus that edge, even when the R prefix created cycles on the departed side.

For r=3, three freshly inserted edges and the old departing fourth edge form a z unit cycle before L. For r=4 the departing edge is the first new edge of the freshly completed z unit cycle. Both L updates are genuine cycle erasures.

On an erasure-free interval every full block thus has r<=2 and a w-bridge L. Inductively the retained active component is an initial-component piece cut only along initial bridges. Original nonbridge cycles remain whole under these cuts, so each L consumes a distinct initial bridge. The w vertices form a simple path; every added edge remains behind and every R-created lifetime stays black through the interval.

With n<=m L steps, R<=2n+4, giving T<=3m+4 and mass<=2m+4. Each w crossing has L1 length2 and physical head is L1 distance1 from its w cursor at both endpoints, giving head displacement<=2m+2, including the terminal run. Consequently a cycle-erasing L occurs by update3m+5, also for m0.

For an arbitrary interval mark full blocks exceptional if r>=3 or L is a w nonbridge. Each such block ends in an erasure, so E<=D, where D counts physical L updates once even if both graphs lose a cycle. Ordinary blocks may erase a z cycle without being marked, which only reduces E. Exact ordinary inheritance gives n_j<=M_j; mass gain per ordinary block<=1 and exceptional<=3 give M_(j+1)<=2M_j+3 and M_j<=(m+3)2^j-3.

Summing E+1 epochs yields T<=3 sum n_j+5E+4<=3(m+3)(2^(E+1)-1)-4E-5<=6(m+3)2^D. Starting mid-run causes no issue: the departing edge is old at the interval block start whenever r<=3. No original black mass or current cycle-rank bound on total erasures is inferred.
scope: All actual finite-support intervals, whole current graphs with all passive components retained. Recurrence and logarithmic lower bound for cycle erasures, not a defect bound, standard104 capture, positive density, finite-state quotient or monotone rank.
